Rashi on Ketubot 41b:11:1.hebrew: נערה שנתפתתה. והצער בתפוסה - והצער נמי לאביה באנוסה. בתפוסה — לישנא דקרא: "ותפשה ושכב עמה" (דברים כב):
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:11:1.english: A young woman who was seduced. And the pain in [the case of] a seized [woman] - And the pain also [belongs] to her father in [the case of] a raped [woman]. "In [the case of] a seized [woman]" [is] the language of the verse: "and he seized her and lay with her" (Deuteronomy 22[:28]).

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:1.hebrew: לא הספיקה לעמוד בדין וכו' - כיון דלא עמדה בדין, לאו ממון הוא להורישו לבניו. ואמרינן לקמן (כתובות דף מג.): אין אדם מוריש לבנו זכות שזכתה לו תורה בבתו, ויליף לה מקרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:1.english: She did not manage to stand in judgment, etc. - Since she did not stand in judgment, it is not [considered] money to bequeath to his sons. And we say later on (Ketubot 43a): A person does not bequeath to his son a right that the Torah granted him regarding his daughter, and [the Gemara] derives it from a verse.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:2.hebrew: מת האב - משעמדה בדין בנערותיה, בין בגרה קודם מיתה בין לא בגרה:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:2.english: The father died - Once she stood in judgment during her maidenhood, whether she reached majority before [his] death or did not reach majority.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:3.english: They belong to the brothers - For once she stood trial, the father acquired them.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:4.hebrew: ר"ש אומר - אע"פ שעמדה בדין, לא הוי ממון דאב להורישו לבניו עד דמטי לידיה, ובגמרא [מב:] יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:12:4.english: Rabbi Shimon says - Even though she stood in judgment, [the money] is not the father's property to bequeath to his sons until it reaches his hand, and in the Gemara (42b) [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:1:1.hebrew: הא מני ר' יוסי הגלילי היא דאמר תם משלם חצי כופר - דדריש להאי "נקי" לדרשה אחריתי — לדמי ולדות, אם נגח אשה ויצאו ילדיה. הלכך, לא הוה ליה לפלוגי בינייהו בכופר. וכי תימא: הוה ליה לפלוגי דהאי פלגא והאי כוליה? ההיא בכלל רישא היא, דקתני: תם משלם חצי נזק ומועד נזק שלם, ותנא בניזקין והוא הדין לכופר:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:1:1.english: According to whose [opinion] is this [taught]? It is [that of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said: An innocuous [ox] pays half ransom - For he expounds this [word] "innocent" for another exposition — regarding payment for miscarried offspring, if [an ox] gored a woman and her children came out. Therefore, [the Tanna] did not need to distinguish between them regarding ransom. And if you will say: [the Tanna] should have distinguished [between them, stating] that this one [pays] half and that one [pays] the whole — that is included in the first clause, which teaches: "An innocuous [ox] pays half damages and a forewarned [ox pays] full damages," and [the Tanna] taught [it] with respect to damages, and the same law applies to ransom.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:2:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בתם - ואי משום דקתני בה המית שורי את פלוני, דחיובו כופר ותם לאו בר כופר הוא — הא מני? רבי יוסי הגלילי היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:2:1.english: What, is [this] not [referring] to an innocuous [ox] - And if [you ask] because it teaches in it, "My ox killed so-and-so," for which the liability is ransom, and an innocuous [ox] is not subject to ransom — whose [opinion] is this? It is [that of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:1.english: Rather than teaching "the slave of so-and-so," etc. - For [the Tanna] did not find [a case of] exemption [from payment] on his own [admission] except regarding a slave.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:2.english: Let him distinguish within [the case] itself - Regarding a free person and an animal as well, [the Tanna] could have drawn a distinction and taught that there is [a case] where he does not pay based on his own [admission].

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:3.hebrew: בד"א - דמשלם ע"פ עצמו, במועד כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:3.english: In what [case] is this statement said - [i.e.,] that he pays based on his own [admission] — in [the case of] a forewarned [ox], etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:4.hebrew: כולה במועד קמיירי - במועד אתא לאשמועי' דאף הוא יש בו חילוק, דאיכא ביה מידי דלא משלם על פי עצמו, ומאי ניהו? נגיחת עבד. ואי הוה תני כדקאמרת, הוה שביק נמי לאורחיה, דרישא איירי במועד וסיפא ניתני תם. ומה לי שבקה תנא לאורחיה גבי ניזק, לדלג מבן חורין לעבד, מה לי שבקה במזיק, ולדלג ממועד לתם:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:3:4.english: The entire [mishna] is speaking of a forewarned [ox] - It comes to teach us regarding a forewarned [ox] that even it has a distinction, for there is a case in it where one does not pay based on his own [admission]. And what is it? Goring a slave. And if [the Tanna] had taught as you said, he would also be departing from his [usual] pattern, since the first clause deals with a forewarned [ox] and the latter clause would teach [about] an innocuous [ox]. And what difference is there to me whether the Tanna departed from his [usual] pattern regarding the injured party, to jump from a free person to a slave, [or] whether he departed from it regarding the damager, to jump from a forewarned [ox] to an innocuous [ox]?

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:4:1.hebrew: יתר על מה שהזיק - כגון נגיחת עבד, וכן אונס ומפתה, ומוציא שם רע, ותשלומי כפל, ותשלומי ארבעה וחמשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:4:1.english: More than what he damaged - For example, the goring of a slave, and likewise a rapist and a seducer, and a defamer, and twofold payment, and fourfold and fivefold payments.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:4:2.english: [If he pays] less than what he damaged - For example, the half-damage [payment] of a *tam* [an innocuous animal].

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:5:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: ליתני כל שאינו משלם כמה שהזיק, אינו משלם <abbr title="על פי">ע"פ</abbr> עצמו:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:5:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: Let [the tanna] teach: "Anyone who does not pay [the amount] that he damaged does not pay based on his own [admission]."

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:1.hebrew: והלכתא פלגא ניזקא קנסא - דהואיל וכל חצי נזק אינו אלא בניזקא דלאו אורחיה, לאו על מריה הוה רמיא למינטריה בהכי, אלא קנסא הוא כי היכי דלוסיף ביה נטירותא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:1.english: And the halakha [is that] half-damage is a fine - For since any half-damage is only for damage that is not its usual manner, it was not incumbent upon its owner to guard it against such [damage]; rather, it is a fine so that he will increase [his] guarding over it.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:2.hebrew: טעמא מאי איתותב - כלומר, תיובתא מאי היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:2.english: What is the reason he was conclusively refuted - That is to say, what is the refutation?

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:3.hebrew: משום דלא קתני כל שאינו משלם כמה שהזיק אינו משלם על פי עצמו - דלישתמע מינה נמי חצי נזק, הא לאו תיובתא היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:3.english: Because [the Tanna] does not teach: Anyone who does not pay as much as he damaged does not pay by his own admission - so that half-damage would also be implied from it, this is not a refutation.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:4.hebrew: כיון דאיכא חצי נזק - דמשתלם בנזקי בהמה במהלכת והתיזה צרורות מתחת רגליה והזיקה, דתנן בבבא קמא (דף יז.) דמשלמת חצי נזק. ובההוא חצי נזק קיימא לן בב"ק דהלכתא גמירי לה מסיני שהוא תולדה של רגל, ופטורה ברה"ר כי רגל; וניזקי רגל לאו קנסא נינהו אלא ממונא, שהרי מועדת מתחילתה, וגבי צרורות הוא דאקיל רחמנא. וכיון דממונא הוא, משלם ע"פ עצמו. משום הכי לא פסיקא ליה למיתני כל שאינו משלם כמה שהזיק, דהא איכא האי:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:6:4.english: Since there is half-damage - which is paid for damages of an animal walking [in its usual manner] that kicked up pebbles from beneath its feet and caused damage, as we learned in a Mishnah in Bava Kamma (17a) that it pays half-damage. And regarding that half-damage, it is established for us in Bava Kamma that it is a law transmitted [to Moses] from Sinai that it is a derivative of Foot [damage], and it is exempt in the public domain like Foot; and Foot damages are not a fine, but rather monetary [compensation], since [an animal] is forewarned [with respect to Foot] from the outset, and it is [only] regarding pebbles that the Merciful One was lenient. And since it is monetary [compensation], one pays on his own admission. Therefore, it was not clear-cut for [the Tanna] to teach "anyone who does not pay the amount that he damaged," because there is this [case].

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:7:1.english: That ate lambs - That strangled live lambs and ate them.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:7:2.hebrew: משונה הוא - אין דרכו בכך, וכל נזק משונה בבהמה הוי תולדה דקרן תמה, שאף היא משונה שאין דרכה בכך, וחצי נזק הוא דמשלם. וכיון דקנסא הוא, לא מגבינן ליה בדייני בבל, שאין שם סמיכה בזקנים ולא מקרו מומחים, וגבי קנס כתיב (שמות כב) "ירשיעון אלהים":
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:7:2.english: It is unusual - It is not its usual manner [to do] so, and any unusual damage by an animal is a subcategory of an innocuous goring ox, for that too is unusual, as it is not its usual manner [to do] so, and it is [only] half-damages that [the owner] pays. And since [half-damages] is a fine, we do not collect it through the judges of Babylonia, for there is no ordination of elders there and they are not called "experts," and regarding a fine it is written (Exodus 22[:8]): "whom the judges [elohim] shall condemn."

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:7:3.hebrew: אורחיה הוא - והוו להו נזקי דשן, ושן משלמת נזק שלם, וממונא הוא, וגובין אותו בבבל:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:7:3.english: It is its usual manner - And [therefore] they are damages of Tooth, and Tooth pays full damages, and it is a monetary [obligation], and we collect it in Babylonia.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:8:1.hebrew: ואי תפס - ניזק ממונא דמזיק גבי קנסא דחצי נזקו, דאין צריך לצעוק לפנינו:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:8:1.english: And if he seized - [If] the injured party [seized] money of the damager regarding the fine of his half-damage, so that he does not need to cry out [for redress] before us.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:8:2.english: We do not take [it] from him - And he collects his half-damage [from it].

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:8:3.hebrew: ואי - לא תפיס, ואמר קמן: "קבעו לי זמנא בארעא דישראל" — השיאוהו לילך עמי לדון לפני דייני ארץ ישראל — קבעינן ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:8:3.english: And if - he did not seize [property], and he said before us, "Set me a time in the Land of Israel" — [meaning,] direct him to go with me to litigate before the judges of the Land of Israel — we set [a time] for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:9:1.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך - בין שרוצה ניזק לילך לארץ ישראל, בין שאינו רוצה:
Rashi on Ketubot 41b:9:1.english: Either way - Whether the injured party wants to go to the Land of Israel, [or] whether he does not want [to].

Rashi on Ketubot 41b:9:2.english: We excommunicate him - the damager, at least, to kill that dog and remove his [cause of] damage.

Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:12:1.hebrew: נערה. לא הספיקה לעמוד בדין עד שמת האב הרי הן של עצמה - תימה: תינח קנס, אלא בושת ופגם דממונא הוא, דאחין בעי למיהוי. ושמא מקראי דלעיל דנפקי בושת ופגם איתקוש אהדדי, כדפי' לעיל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:12:1.english: [Mishnah:] "A young woman." [If] she did not manage to stand in judgment before the father died, they belong to her. - [This is] difficult: That is well [regarding] the fine, but [regarding] humiliation and degradation, which are monetary [compensation], they ought to belong to the brothers. And perhaps, from the verses above from which humiliation and degradation are derived, they are compared to one another, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:1:1.hebrew: הא מני רבי יוסי הגלילי היא דאמר תם משלם חצי כופר - וליכא שיורא, דאי משום דמועד משלם כופר שלם ותם אינו משלם אלא חצי כופר — הא לאו שיורא הוא, דהא תנן: תם משלם חצי נזק ומועד נזק שלם, וכופר בכלל. וא"ת: אכתי ליתני דמועד אף כשהוא בסקילה משלם כופר, ותם כשהוא בסקילה אינו משלם כופר כלל, דהביאהו לב"ד וישלם לך, דהוא עצמו אינו משתלם אלא מגופו, כדאמרינן בפרק שור שנגח ד' וה' (ב"ק דף מב. ושם)! וי"ל דהך נמי לא הוי שיור, דהוי בכלל הא דקתני: תם מגופו ומועד מן העלייה. ומיהו תימה, דלא אשכחן בהדיא בשום מקום שהיה אומר ר' יוסי הגלילי דתם משלם חצי כופר; ואי משום דדריש רבי יוסי הגלילי בפרק שור שנגח ד' וה' (ג"ז שם) "נקי" מדמי ולדות ולא דריש "נקי" מחצי כופר, מכלל דסבר דחייב — ודלמא לעולם סבר דפטור, וטעמא משום דפטור מחצי כופר לא איצטריך קרא, דכשהשור בסקילה לא שייך כופר, דהביאהו לב"ד וישלם לך, וכשאין השור בסקילה, כגון על פי עד אחד או על פי הבעלים, פטור מדרבה, דאמר התם (דף מג.) [ שור שהמית בן חורין שלא בכוונה פטור, שנאמר: "השור יסקל וגם בעליו יומת", בזמן שהשור בסקילה — בעלים משלמין כופר כו'. ונראה דה"פ: "הא מני? ר' יוסי הגלילי היא, דאמר: תם משלם חצי כופר", פי' דלא ממעט חצי כופר מ"נקי", ולאו דוקא "משלם" קאמר, אלא היה משלם אם היה לו ממה להשתלם. ולשום תנא לא הוה חצי כופר שיור, כי אם לרבי אלעזר, דדריש "נקי" מחצי כופר ולית ליה דרבה, וכשאין השור בסקילה מועד משלם ותם אינו משלם. והא דנקט רבי יוסי הגלילי טפי מרבי עקיבא, דדריש "נקי" מדמי עבד — דלדידיה, נהי דחצי כופר לא הוי שיור, דמי עבד הוי שיור:
Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:1:1.english: "Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said: An innocuous [ox] pays half ransom." - And there is no omission [in the Mishnah]; for if [one might argue that it omitted] that a forewarned [ox] pays full ransom whereas an innocuous [ox] pays only half ransom — this is not an omission, for we learned [in the Mishnah]: An innocuous [ox] pays half-damages and a forewarned [ox] [pays] full damages, and ransom is included [in this]. And if you should say: Still, let [the Mishnah] teach that a forewarned [ox], even when it is [subject to] stoning, pays ransom, whereas an innocuous [ox], when it is [subject to] stoning, does not pay ransom at all, because [one says to the claimant:] "Bring it to court and it will pay you," as it itself is paid only from its own body, as we say in the chapter "An ox that gored four or five" (Bava Kamma 42a, and there)! One can answer that this too is not an omission, for it is included in that which [the Mishnah] teaches: "An innocuous [ox pays] from its own body, and a forewarned [ox] from the best [property]." However, it is astonishing, for we do not find explicitly anywhere that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said that an innocuous [ox] pays half ransom! And if [you say this is inferred] because Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounds in the chapter "An ox that gored four or five" (ibid.) [the word] "clean" [as exempting] from payment for miscarried fetuses, and does not expound "clean" [as exempting] from half ransom, which implies that he holds that it is liable — perhaps in fact he holds that it is exempt, and the reason [a verse was not needed] is because to exempt [it] from half ransom no verse is needed! For when the ox is [subject to] stoning, ransom does not apply, because [of the principle] "Bring it to court and it will pay you"; and when the ox is not [subject to] stoning, such as [when convicted] on the testimony of a single witness or by the owner's [admission], it is exempt according to Rabbah, who said there (43a): "An ox that killed a free person unintentionally is exempt, as it is stated: 'The ox shall be stoned, and also its owner shall be put to death' — when the ox is [subject to] stoning, the owner pays ransom, etc." And it appears that this is its explanation: "Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said: An innocuous [ox] pays half ransom" — meaning that he does not exclude half ransom from [the word] "clean," and he does not literally mean "pays," rather it would pay if it had from what to be paid. And according to no Tanna is half ransom an omission, except for Rabbi Elazar, who expounds "clean" [as exempting] from half ransom and does not hold [the ruling] of Rabbah, so when the ox is not [subject to] stoning, a forewarned [ox] pays and an innocuous [ox] does not pay. And the reason [the Gemara] cited Rabbi Yosei HaGelili rather than Rabbi Akiva, who expounds "clean" [as exempting] from payment for a slave — [is because] according to him, granted that half ransom is not an omission, payment for a slave would be an omission:

Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:8:1.hebrew: ואי תפס כו' - פר"ת דדוקא אי תפס את המזיק עצמו, אבל דבר אחר לא; דלענין מזיק עצמו הקילו חכמים שיכול לתופסו, דאל"כ יתפוס כל אשר לו ולא נפיק מיניה, דאין דנין דיני קנסות, ואם נוציא המותר ונשאיר כדי נזק — הרי אנו דנין דיני קנסות. ודוחק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 41b:8:1.english: And if he seized, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam explained that [this applies] specifically if he seized the damager itself, but not something else; for with respect to the damager itself, the Sages were lenient [in ruling] that he may seize it, for otherwise he would seize all that he has and we would not repossess [it] from him, since we do not adjudicate cases of fines — and if we were to repossess the excess and leave [only] the amount of the damage, we would thereby be adjudicating cases of fines. And [this explanation is] forced.
